key_insight: Graph neural networks now serve as a general framework for learning from relational data across many domains, but their value depends heavily on whether graph structure truly adds signal beyond added complexity.
clinical_relevance: For healthcare and neuroscience applications, GNNs can help model complex relationships in patient, molecular, and brain data, yet deployment requires careful validation because performance gains may not transfer under real-world data shift or heterophily.
method: Derives spectral and spatial GNN formulations from shared first principles.
Maps model expressiveness to the Weisfeiler-Leman hierarchy.
Reviews 12 application domains with graph-construction, architecture, and baseline considerations.
evidence_signal: The survey synthesizes comparative findings across multiple domains and emphasizes that reported gains can be inflated by weak baselines, favorable splits, or mismatched evaluation settings.
watch_item: Temporal graphs, distribution shift, and fairness/explainability remain major implementation concerns, so strong leaderboard performance does not guarantee clinical usefulness.
paper_title: Graph Neural Networks Applications Across Domains: All Insights You Need
